bug_semantics: FRR bgpd process_type2_route in bgpd/bgp_evpn.c accepts an EVPN Type-2 NLRI whose overall length psize is one of {33,36,37,40,49,52} and whose inner IP-length field is independently 0, 32, or 128, without requiring psize == 33+(ipaddr_len/8) or psize == 36+(ipaddr_len/8). A remote EVPN BGP speaker can therefore present a legal total length while declaring a mismatched IP length so that IP octets are consumed as MPLS/VNI labels or leftover bytes are treated as a second VNI, installing a MAC-IP route with the wrong IP and/or VNI. After the 2020 STREAM_GET conversion, over-reads fail closed, but the inconsistent-length path still yields a wrongly decoded route rather than a reject. CVE-2026-5107/VulDB label this CWE-266/CWE-284; the concrete flaw is missing NLRI-length vs IP-length cross-validation in Type-2 parsing.
flaw_origin: The missing consistency check was first written when Vivek Venkatraman added process_type2_route in 128ea8abbd38eddd2a9bfa18b596acd95f081353 (2017-05-15 / committed 2017-07-12). That commit introduced the psize whitelist and independent ipaddr_len read/copy with no cross-check. Parent 0ee26848f37d44ca5f1285e05f06bedd975a851c has neither the function nor Type-2 NLRI parsing. Later refactors (e121d831 STREAM_GET conversion; field-name/style edits) preserved the same gap until 7676cad65114aa23adde583d91d9d29e2debd045 added the psize vs ipaddr_len guard.
